question: Which body system uses chemical messengers (hormones) sent through the bloodstream to cause slow, long-lasting changes?
explanation: Hormones are released by endocrine glands and travel through the blood to target organs. This creates a slower, longer-lasting response compared to fast nerve impulses. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why do endocrine signals take longer to work than nerve signals?

options.A: Hormones must travel through the bloodstream to reach target tissues
options.B: Endocrine glands store very little chemical substance
options.C: Target cells actively block incoming hormones at first
options.D: Nerve impulses move slower than liquid blood flow

explanation: Circulation time determines how long it takes for a hormone to reach its specific receptor site, making the response more gradual than electrical nerve signals. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which part of the brain is the main link between the nervous system and the endocrine system?
explanation: The hypothalamus receives signals from various parts of the brain and releases hormones that control the pituitary gland. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h2)

question: A blockage in which specific blood vessel network would immediately stop hypothalamic hormones from reaching the anterior pituitary?
explanation: The hypophysial portal system carries blood directly from the hypothalamus to the anterior pituitary, ensuring high hormone concentrations reach the target cells. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h2)

question: How must Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) be released from the hypothalamus to keep the pituitary working normally?

options.A: In response to high uterine pressure

explanation: Pulsatile secretion prevents receptor downregulation, which happens when pituitary cells are exposed to constant, uninterrupted hormone levels. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h3)

question: What happens to pituitary hormone production if a patient receives continuous, non-stop synthetic GnRH for a long time?

options.A: It shifts to producing only prolactin
options.B: It accelerates the onset of ovulation
options.C: It increases to dangerously high levels
options.D: It becomes suppressed or shut down

explanation: Constant exposure desensitizes the pituitary receptors, causing a drop in FSH and LH release, which is used therapeutically to suppress sex hormone production. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which anterior pituitary hormone is mainly responsible for triggering ovulation mid-cycle?
explanation: A sharp, massive surge of LH from the anterior pituitary directly causes the mature follicle to rupture and release the egg. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the main job of FSH during the first half of the menstrual cycle (the follicular phase)?

options.A: Maintaining the endometrial lining after implantation
options.B: Stopping all estrogen production in the ovaries
options.C: Causing immediate degeneration of the corpus luteum
options.D: Promoting the growth and recruitment of ovarian follicles

explanation: FSH stimulates a group of ovarian follicles to grow, helping select the dominant follicle that will move on to ovulation. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which hormone is produced in large amounts by the corpus luteum after ovulation to prepare the uterine lining?
explanation: The corpus luteum secretes abundant progesterone, which changes the uterine lining into a secretory, nutrient-rich bed ready for a fertilized egg. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why do theca cells and granulosa cells need to work together to make estrogen?

options.A: Granulosa cells cannot survive without direct physical touch from theca cells
options.B: Theca cells make androgens that granulosa cells must convert into estrogen
options.C: Theca cells block FSH from entering the ovarian tissue
options.D: Granulosa cells produce all the necessary cholesterol without outside help

explanation: Neither cell type alone has all the enzymes needed to make estrogen from scratch. Theca cells make the starting androgens, and granulosa cells convert them into estrogen. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h5)

question: What triggers the mid-cycle LH surge through positive feedback?

options.A: Complete absence of gonadotropins in the blood
options.B: Sustained high levels of estrogen from the mature follicle
options.C: A sudden drop in core body temperature
options.D: High levels of progesterone secreted by immature follicles

explanation: Unlike the rest of the cycle where estrogen suppresses hormone release, peak estrogen levels paradoxically trigger a burst of GnRH and LH. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a function of negative feedback during the normal menstrual cycle?

options.A: Causing the mid-cycle LH surge that forces ovulation
options.B: Preventing the development of new follicles while the corpus luteum is active
options.C: Suppressing excessive FSH release during the luteal phase
options.D: Keeping baseline gonadotropin levels low in the early follicular phase

explanation: The mid-cycle surge is driven by positive feedback. Negative feedback is used to suppress and control hormone levels at other times in the cycle. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h6)
